copyright: Rainbow Falls on the Wailuku River, Hilo, Hawaii, USA (© Peter Unger/Getty Images)
description: Water, sunlight and lush greenery come together at Rainbow Falls in Hilo, on the island of Hawaii. Here, the Wailuku River plunges around 24 metres over a lava ledge, sending mist into the air as it reaches the pool below. On sunny mornings, the mist can catch the light and produce the colourful rainbows that gave the falls their name. Known in Hawaiian as Waiānuenue, meaning 'rainbow water', this striking waterfall is surrounded by tropical vegetation and has a special place in Hawaiian legend.

copyright: Sunset Point, Bryce Canyon National Park, Utah, USA (© Colin D. Young/Alamy)
description: Snow transforms Bryce Canyon National Park, blanketing the landscape in white while its fiery orange-red hoodoos rise above the snowy terrain. Seen from Sunset Point, one of the park's best-known viewpoints, these fantastical shapes are part of the Claron Formation, a collection of sedimentary rocks deposited around 50 million years ago and later sculpted by weathering and erosion. Because much of the park lies above 2,440 metres, snow can arrive as early as October. In today's image, snow clings to the canyon's ridges and spires while mist drifts across the cliffs, creating an iconic winter scene in the American Southwest.

copyright: Red squirrel in Cairngorms National Park, Highlands, Scotland (© Scotland: The Big Picture/Minden Pictures)
description: As Britain's only native squirrel species, red squirrels thrive in Scotland's Cairngorms National Park. An important refuge, the park offers ancient Caledonian pine forests and more recently planted conifer woodlands, providing valuable habitat and food for squirrels foraging for Scots pine seeds, nuts and other tasty morsels throughout the year. In today's image, a red squirrel is perched amid warm orange and yellow leaves, looking right at home as it ponders its next move in the Scottish Highlands.

Today's image shows the gradual coiling of a young fiddlehead's tip, echoing the geometric patterns seen throughout nature. In maths, the Fibonacci sequence follows a similar progression, each number formed by adding the two before it: 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8 and so on. Today is Fibonacci Day, chosen for the numbers of the date (11/23) to honour the sequence. Eventually the young fern frond shown here will unfurl as it grows, but elsewhere in the plant world, the sequence will continue to appear in the spiralling arrangements of sunflower heads, pinecones, succulents and pineapples.

copyright: The chapel and hermitage of Santa Justa in Cantabria, Spain (© Tramont_ana/Getty Images)
description: Tucked into the rugged coastline of northern Spain, the 16th-century Hermitage of Santa Justa, featured in today's image, overlooks the crashing waves of the Cantabrian Sea. Built partly into the rock and associated with the relics of Saints Justa and Rufina, the small chapel eventually became a pilgrimage site. Its sheltered stone walls create a striking contrast with the powerful waves and rugged cliffs around it.

copyright: Nice, Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur, France (© Siripong Kaewla-iad/Getty Images)
description: Bathed in a sun-kissed glow, Nice is a patchwork of terracotta rooftops, historic churches and pastel façades along the French Riviera, as seen in today's image. Founded by the ancient Greeks and long associated with the Italian House of Savoy, Nice officially became part of France in 1860. Today, its layered past remains visible throughout this coastal city in the south of France, where historic architecture meets the blue waters of the Mediterranean and the sunlit hills of the Côte d'Azur.

copyright: Diving humpback whale, Kvaloya, Troms, Northern Norway (© Espen Bergersen/Minden Pictures)
description: Off the coast of Kvaløya in Troms, northern Norway, humpback whales move through the cold Arctic waters in search of a proper feast. They visit the region in winter, following migrating herring into the fjords. Humpbacks are known for their remarkable feeding techniques, including bubble-net feeding, in which some whales blow rings or walls of bubbles to corral fish before surging upwards with their mouths open to catch their prey. In today's image, a humpback slips beneath the icy waves under a glowing pastel sky, capturing a moment of tranquillity in Norway's wild north.
